summary.en: Use the **passive** when the action matters more than who does it, or when we don't know or don't need to say who did it. Form it with **be + past participle**, and change the tense of **be**: _The bridge is repaired every year_, _was built in 1990_, _has been closed_. Add **by + agent** only when the doer is useful information.
summary.es: En inglés la pasiva se usa mucho más que en español, donde a menudo decimos «se arregla» o «arreglan». Siempre lleva el verbo **be** y el participio: no se puede omitir ninguno de los dos.

form: Present perfect: **has/have been + past participle** (_has been made_)
Future: **will be + past participle**; with modals: **can/must/should be + past participle**
Continuous: **is being / was being + past participle** (_is being repaired_)
Negative and questions follow the auxiliary: _It wasn't finished._ _Was it finished?_

uses.text: **The doer is unknown or unimportant**: _My bike **was stolen** last night._
**The action or result is the focus**: _The new library **will be opened** in May._
**General facts and processes**: _Olive oil **is produced** in many parts of Spain._
**Naming the doer with by**: _The report **was written by** an independent team._

note.en: Use by only when the doer adds information. Don't say by people or by someone.
note.es: Usa by solo si el agente aporta información; no se dice by people ni by someone.

uses.text: **Verbs with two objects** can have two passives: _She was given a pay rise_ or _A pay rise was given to her._

why.en: A passive needs be + past participle. Without been, the verb sounds active.
why.es: La pasiva necesita be en el tiempo correcto: has been cancelled, no has cancelled.

mistakes.wrong: English is spoken in many countries by people.
mistakes.right: English is spoken in many countries.

why.en: Leave out the agent when it is obvious or general.
why.es: No añadas by people: el agente obvio se omite.

mistakes.wrong: The road is repairing at the moment.
mistakes.right: The road is being repaired at the moment.

why.en: The present continuous passive is is/are being + past participle.
why.es: «Se está arreglando» es is being repaired, no is repairing.

why.en: Verbs like happen, arrive, die and seem have no object, so they have no passive.
why.es: Los verbos intransitivos (happen, arrive, die) no tienen pasiva.

examples.en: The tickets are sold online only.
examples.es: Las entradas se venden solo por internet.

examples.en: This church was designed by a local architect in 1862.
examples.es: Esta iglesia fue diseñada por un arquitecto local en 1862.

examples.en: Several roads have been closed because of the flooding.
examples.es: Se han cortado varias carreteras por las inundaciones.

examples.en: Your order will be delivered within three working days.
The town hall is being renovated, so it's closed until June.
Mobile phones must not be used during the exam.
I was offered a job in Dublin, but I turned it down.
Was the package signed for, or was it left outside?
The suspect hasn't been found yet.
Glass should be recycled, not thrown away.

practice.prompt: The windows ___ every month by a cleaning company.

explanation.en: The windows receive the action, so we need the passive: are cleaned.

practice.prompt: Sorry about the noise: the street ___ at the moment.

explanation.en: An action in progress now needs the continuous passive: is being repaired.

practice.prompt: My laptop ___ from my car last week.

explanation.en: Last week is a finished time, so the past simple passive is needed: was stolen.

practice.prompt: All the staff ___ about the changes by email tomorrow.

explanation.en: The staff receive the information, so the future passive is will be informed.
